answer: On an island, an agent cooperative holds one simultaneous registration hour at staffed venues, from the wharf to an onyx-floored town hall. Operators must stay physically present throughout. Staff register one agent key per person and issue one single-use ballot token for the round. Extra aliases cannot put one body in two venues at once or multiply its voting weight. This relies on honest staff and synchronized sessions; hired stand-ins or corrupt issuers can still add votes, and travel excludes some honest operators.
